title: Corporate Wellness Partnership: billing cycle day, late-payment grace, and suspension terms by tier
content:
This document covers the Corporate Wellness Partnership's monthly billing-cycle day for the employer's master account, the grace period before a missed payment is treated as late, the flat late-payment fee amount, the number of consecutive missed billing cycles that triggers suspension, whether suspension happens automatically on the employer's nonpayment, and the notice given to the employee before their enrollment is suspended for that reason.

| Tier | Monthly billing day | Grace period before a payment is late | Flat late-payment fee amount | Consecutive missed cycles that trigger suspension | Suspends automatically on employer nonpayment | Employee notice before suspension |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Startup Partner | Day 1 of the month | 15 calendar days | $50.00 | 2 | Yes | 7 calendar days |
| Small Business Partner | Day 1 of the month | 15 calendar days | $75.00 | 2 | Yes | 10 calendar days |
| Mid-Market Partner | Day 1 of the month | 20 calendar days | $100.00 | 2 | Yes | 14 calendar days |
| Enterprise Partner | Day 1 of the month | 30 calendar days | $150.00 | 3 | Yes | 21 calendar days |
| Municipal Partner | Day 1 of the month | 30 calendar days | $0.00 | 3 | No | 21 calendar days |
| Nonprofit Partner | Day 1 of the month | 30 calendar days | $0.00 | 3 | No | 21 calendar days |

The late-payment fee amount shown here sizes the current per-cycle late-payment charge; how many cycles it applies to, and how that charge is calculated and assessed, is stated in a separate document. Suspension itself follows once the tier's number of consecutive billing cycles has gone unpaid where automatic suspension on employer nonpayment applies to that tier; where it does not apply, the employer's master account may fall behind without the enrollment itself moving to suspended status on that basis alone.
